deep.reconstruction:
The page is a compact formula sheet ('Trigonometria sphaerica') with no derivations. The next page gives the plane analogue ('Praecepta trigonometrica / Trigonometria plana'). The previous page holds the half-angle analogies (Delambre/Gauss analogies). Conventions: sides a, b, c are opposite angles A, B, C. In the right-angled section, h is the hypotenuse, a and b are the legs, the right angle is C, and leg b is adjacent to A.

I. Triangula rectangula (right spherical triangles):
(1) cos h = cos a cos b (spherical Pythagoras).
(2) cos h = cot A cot B, written as cos h tan A tan B = 1.
(3) sin a = sin h sin A.
(4) tan b = tan h cos A.
(5) tan b = sin a tan B.
(6) cos A = cos a sin B.
These six relations are the full set of Napier's rules (the remaining four follow by swapping a,A with b,B).

II. Triangula obliquangula (general spherical triangles). Write s = (a+b+c)/2; this abbreviation is mine.
(1) Sine law: sin A sin b = sin B sin a.
(2) Side cosine law: cos a = cos b cos c + sin b sin c cos A.
(3) Half-angle sine: sin(A/2) = sqrt( sin(s-c) sin(s-b) / (sin b sin c) ), since (a+b-c)/2 = s-c and (a-b+c)/2 = s-b.
(4) Half-angle cosine: cos(A/2) = sqrt( sin s sin(s-a) / (sin b sin c) ).
(5) sin A = 2 sin(A/2) cos(A/2) = sqrt( 4 sin s sin(s-a) sin(s-b) sin(s-c) / (sin^2 b sin^2 c) ). This is the implicit step: multiply (3) by (4) and double.
(6) tan B = sin A / (sin c cot b - cos A cos c). This is the cotangent (four-part) formula cot b sin c = cos c cos A + sin A cot B, solved for B. It gives B from two sides and the included angle (b, c, A).
(7) and (8) Napier's analogies:
- tan((A+B)/2) = cos((a-b)/2) cot(C/2) / cos((a+b)/2)
- tan((A-B)/2) = sin((a-b)/2) cot(C/2) / sin((a+b)/2)
These also serve the case of two sides and the included angle.
(9) Polar (angle) cosine law: cos A = cos a sin B sin C - cos B cos C.
(10)-(12) are stated only verbally: analogous formulas for sin(a/2), cos(a/2) and sin a. By polarity (my completion), with S = (A+B+C)/2:
- sin(a/2) = sqrt( -cos S cos(S-A) / (sin B sin C) )
- cos(a/2) = sqrt( cos(S-B) cos(S-C) / (sin B sin C) )
- sin a = their doubled product.

At the bottom are stray scribbles ('90°+a-b', 'a', '90-b/2' (?), '90-b'). They look like trial angle substitutions (complements, possibly polar-triangle replacements) and carry no recoverable derivation.

Purpose: a reference sheet for solving spherical triangles in all standard cases, paired with the plane sheet on the next page. It is didactic or practical (geodetic/astronomical computing) in character.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All 15 written formulas are correct under the conventions stated (for right triangles: h hypotenuse, C = 90°, leg b adjacent to A).
Formulas (10)-(12) are only announced, not written out. The direct analogy 'similes ut (3)(4)(5)' hides the sign change: sin(a/2) involves -cos S, which is positive because pi < 2S < 3pi.
In (7) and (8) the leading '+' signs, written right under the '=' sign, are superfluous. They may be a vestigial or partly formed ± mark; the formulas are correct with +.
The square-root forms (3)-(5) do not state the sign convention; all the quantities are positive for proper (Eulerian) triangles.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard textbook summary of spherical trigonometry, entirely classical by Gauss's time and fully correct. The only Gauss-associated material (the Gauss/Delambre analogies) is on the previous page, not here.
